title: Choose the chat screen's structure
question: Three layouts for conversations + chat, all in Loom's palette (indigo warp, madder weft, linen ground). Lock one, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: Prompts in the margin
options.thesis: Your prompts sit in a narrow left margin beside the reply they produced, so the reply owns the full reading measure.
materials: madder thread joining prompt to reply
options.viewport: Indigo sidebar left; transcript as two columns, prompts at 240px in the margin, replies at 68ch; composer docked bottom under the reply column.
options.risk: Long prompts get tall in a narrow margin; edits happen in a cramped column.

options.label: Familiar column + weave rail
options.thesis: The chat layout everyone knows, plus a thin right rail that draws the conversation as warp and weft: one mark per turn, branch points visible at a glance.
options.viewport: Indigo sidebar left; centered 720px column with user turns as linen-dark blocks; 56px weave rail right; composer docked bottom.
options.risk: The rail is new vocabulary; it has to earn its width by being clickable navigation, not decoration.

options.label: Three panes with inspector
options.thesis: Conversations, transcript, and an inspector that shows the machinery of the selected turn: model, tokens, stop reason, versions.
options.viewport: Indigo sidebar left; transcript center; 300px inspector right showing the selected reply's model, input/output tokens, stop reason and sibling versions.
options.risk: Inspector shows only per-message data today; the real context/budget view needs API work, so it may feel thin until then.
